backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, initialize radii based on the target sum of radii divided by n, or a small fraction of the average distance between random points.
backlog.title: Initial Radius Scaling

backlog.spec: Start with very small radii and, during optimization, prioritize increasing the radii of circles that are not currently in contact with others.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Initialize the problem with very small radii (where constraints are easily satisfied) and slowly increase the target sum of radii as a parameter in the objective function.
backlog.title: Gradual Constraint Relaxation

backlog.spec: Use a simulated annealing approach where the 'temperature' controls the acceptance of moves that slightly decrease the sum of radii but improve the packing feasibility.
backlog.title: Multi-Start Local Search with Temperature

backlog.spec: Rewrite the objective to be -sum(r) + lambda * sum(max(0, overlap)), where lambda is increased over time to enforce hard constraints.
backlog.title: Penalty Method instead of Constraints

backlog.spec: Modify the repair function to use a more robust shrinking factor, such as 0.95, instead of a direct ratio, and run it until the overlap is below a very small epsilon.
backlog.title: Better Repair - Iterative Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Use a greedy 'best-fit' placement to initialize the circles: place circles one by one in the first available spot that doesn't overlap.
backlog.title: Sphere Packing Initialization

backlog.spec: After each iteration of SLSQP, add a very small amount of Gaussian noise to the centers to help escape local optima, then continue optimization.
backlog.title: Coordinate Jittering

backlog.spec: Instead of fixed restarts, spend more time on a single optimization if the rate of improvement in the sum of radii starts to slow down.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Budgeting

backlog.spec: Add a penalty to the objective function if any radius exceeds a value that would make the circle exceed the [0,1] boundary, rather than relying solely on constraints.
backlog.title: Soft Radius Bounds

backlog.spec: Initialize centers by sampling points from a Voronoi tessellation of a random set of points, ensuring a more even distribution.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based Initialization

backlog.spec: Phase 1: Optimize only centers to maximize the minimum distance between any two points. Phase 2: Optimize radii given those fixed centers.
backlog.title: Two-Phase Optimization

backlog.spec: Calculate the gradient of the sum of radii with respect to the centers and radii, and perform manual steps (e.g., Adam) before calling SLSQP.
backlog.title: Gradient-based Radius Adjustment

backlog.spec: Decrease INIT_LOW as the optimization progresses to allow circles to move closer to the boundaries of the unit square.
backlog.title: Dynamic INIT_LOW

backlog.spec: Change the objective to maximize sum(r) - M * sum(overlaps), where M is a large constant. This avoids the complexity of the constraint Jacobian for overlaps.
backlog.title: Overlap-based Objective

backlog.spec: Introduce a distribution for initial radii (e.g., log-normal) so that some circles are intentionally larger than others.
backlog.title: Circle Size Diversity

backlog.spec: In the repair step, if a circle exceeds the boundary, move its center toward the center of the square while shrinking its radius.
backlog.title: Boundary-Aware Repair

backlog.spec: Run a short SLSQP (e.g., 50 iterations) to find a local optimum, then perform a random restart, repeating until the time limit.
backlog.title: Nested SLSQP

backlog.spec: Assign higher weights to smaller circles in the objective function to encourage a more diverse and dense packing.
backlog.title: Variable Radius Weights

backlog.spec: Fix the radii once they reach a certain proportion of the optimal sum, and then only optimize the centers to resolve overlaps.
backlog.title: Center-only Movement

backlog.spec: After finding a valid packing with SLSQP, attempt to increase all radii uniformly by a small epsilon and run a few iterations of SLSQP to fix overlaps.
backlog.title: Radial Expansion Step

backlog.spec: Keep track of the best center configurations found and use them as starting points for subsequent optimizations with different radii.
backlog.title: Randomized Restart with Memory

backlog.spec: Explicitly include box constraints [r, 1-r] for center coordinates in the SLSQP call to ensure circles stay inside the square.
backlog.title: Box Constraint Enforcement

backlog.spec: In the repair function, instead of shrinking radii until no overlap, shrink them until the 'energy' (sum of overlaps) is below a threshold.
backlog.title: Soft Repair

backlog.spec: Vectorize the constraint function more aggressively to allow for more complex constraints (like higher-order interactions) without speed penalties.
backlog.title: Parallel Objective Evaluation

backlog.spec: In the repair loop, make the shrinkage factor 's' dependent on the magnitude of the overlap to reach feasibility faster.
backlog.title: Adaptive Shrink Factor

backlog.spec: Run the repair function multiple times with different random shrinkage patterns and keep the best valid result.
backlog.title: Multi-Seed Repair

backlog.spec: Initialize centers using a Poisson Disc Sampling method to ensure no two points are too close at the start.
backlog.title: Density-based Initialization

backlog.spec: Scale MAX_ITER based on the remaining time in the 30s window to ensure we maximize work done per solve.
backlog.title: Time-proportional Iterations

backlog.spec: Constrain the radii such that r_i / r_j is bounded (e.g., between 0.1 and 10.0) to prevent extremely small or large circles from dominating.
backlog.title: Radius Proportionality

backlog.spec: Refine the _repair function to be more robust. Instead of shrinking the most overlapping pair by a fixed ratio, iteratively identify all overlapping pairs and shrink all of them by a small factor (e.g., 0.95) until the number of overlaps is zero. This prevents one circle from 'bullying' another's space and can lead to a more globally balanced packing.
backlog.title: Iterative Shrinkage Repair

backlog.spec: Split the SLSQP solve into two phases. Phase 1: Optimize only the centers (x, y) while keeping radii fixed at a set of values that satisfy the packing. Phase 2: Fix the centers and optimize only the radii. This separates the degrees of freedom and may help the solver find better local optima for the radii.
backlog.title: Two-Phase Radius Optimization

backlog.spec: Start the optimization with all radii set to very small values (e.g., 0.01) and a large number of iterations. Gradually increase the target radii while running shorter SLSQP bursts. This 'growth' approach can help escape local minima where circles are jammed in suboptimal positions.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: After each successful SLSQP call, apply a small random 'jitter' (Gaussian noise with a very small standard deviation) to the circle centers and re-run the optimizer for a few iterations. This helps the solver 'shake' out of narrow local minima in the non-convex landscape.
backlog.title: Coordinate Jittering

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function to check if a circle is overlapping with the boundary (0,1) and the neighboring circles simultaneously. If a circle is 'squeezed' between two others and a wall, prioritize shrinking the circle that has the most constraints on it.
backlog.title: Boundary-Aware Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed MAX_ITER, dynamically calculate the number of iterations allowed for each SLSQP call based on the remaining time in the solve() function. This ensures the script utilizes the full 30s budget effectively across its restarts.
backlog.title: Time-proportional Iterations

backlog.spec: Add a penalty term to the objective function that penalizes radii for being too large or too small (e.g., encouraging a distribution of sizes). This can be used to prevent the optimizer from converging to a degenerate solution where one circle is massive and 31 are tiny.
backlog.title: Soft Radius Bounds

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random centers, use a simple Voronoi-like initialization. Place $n$ points randomly, then move them slightly to maximize the minimum distance between any two points before starting the SLSQP optimization. This provides a much 'cleaner' starting configuration.
backlog.title: Voronoi-based Initialization

backlog.spec: Introduce a weight vector $w$ of size $n$ that scales each radius (radius $i$ is $r_i 	imes w_i$). Optimize the centers and the weights $w$ simultaneously. This allows the solver to 'choose' which circles should be large and which should be small to fill gaps more efficiently.
backlog.title: Radius Proportionality

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, if an overlap is found, instead of just shrinking the two circles involved, identify the circle with the largest radius in the overlap group and shrink it by a slightly larger percentage. Repeat this until the overlap is gone.
backlog.title: Multi-Seed Repair

backlog.spec: Improve the _repair function to handle multiple overlaps more efficiently. Instead of just fixing the first maximum overlap found, identify all pairs with positive overlap and shrink the radii of all circles involved proportionally to their contribution to the overlap until all constraints are satisfied. This should be done iteratively (e.g., for 100 iterations) to ensure convergence to a valid state.
backlog.title: Iterative Shrinkage Repair

backlog.spec: Split the optimization into two distinct phases. Phase 1: Fix the radii to a set of values that are relatively large but likely to allow a packing, and optimize only the centers. Phase 2: Fix the centers found in Phase 1 and perform a dedicated optimization (or a linear sub-problem) to expand the radii as much as possible without violating the non-overlap constraints.
backlog.title: Two-Phase Optimization

backlog.spec: Add a regularization term to the objective function: minimize -(sum(radii) - lambda * sum(radii^2)). This penalizes extremely large radii and encourages a more balanced distribution of sizes, which can sometimes lead to more stable packings in the SLSQP solver. The lambda should be small enough not to significantly shift the optimum.
backlog.title: Soft Radius Bounds

backlog.spec: Add a constraint or a soft penalty that encourages the radii to be somewhat proportional to their local 'available space'. Alternatively, initialize the radii such that they are all equal, and then allow the optimizer to diverge from equality, but penalize very large discrepancies between the smallest and largest radii to prevent 'monopolizing' the space with one huge circle.
backlog.title: Radius Proportionality

backlog.spec: Implement a dynamic time limit for the SLSQP solver. Use a larger MAX_ITER for the first 50% of the time budget to find a good global structure, and then use a smaller MAX_ITER with very small steps (higher precision) for the remaining 50% to 'polish' the positions of the circles.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Budgeting

backlog.spec: Modify the objective or the repair step to use a batch-processing approach. Instead of finding one maximum overlap and fixing it, calculate the total 'overlap energy' (the sum of all pairwise overlaps) and perform a gradient-descent-like step on the radii to minimize this energy quickly before handing it back to SLSQP.
backlog.title: Batch Overlap Check

backlog.spec: Instead of starting with all radii at a uniform INIT_RADIUS, initialize the radii from a distribution that favors a mix of large and small circles (e.g., a power-law or a skewed normal distribution). A mix of sizes often fills the 'gaps' left by large circles more effectively than a uniform distribution.
backlog.title: Circle Size Diversity

backlog.spec: Perform a multi-start search where the radii are fixed to their current 'best' values, and the centers are optimized using a robust local search (like a faster SLSQP or even a simple coordinate descent). Once a very tight packing is found for those radii, re-enable radius growth for a final refinement step.
backlog.title: Center-only Movement

backlog.spec: Since the objective is to maximize the sum of radii, the gradient with respect to $r_i$ is 1. However, the constraints are $d_{ij} 	iminus (r_i + r_j) 	iminus 	ext{const}$. Calculate the dual variables (Lagrange multipliers) for the non-overlap constraints from the SLSQP result. Use these to perform a final linear programming step to push the radii to their maximum possible limits given the final centers.
backlog.title: Gradient-based Radius Adjustment

backlog.spec: In the restart loop, if a configuration is found that is significantly worse than the current best but has a high 'packing density' (sum of radii), there is a small probability to perform a 'swap'. Choose the smallest circle and the largest 'empty' area (found by sampling many points and finding the point furthest from all circle boundaries) and attempt to move the smallest circle to that location. This helps jump between local optima by relocating small circles to fill gaps.
backlog.title: Basin-Hopping Large Circle Swap

backlog.spec: Instead of just maximizing the sum of radii, add a 'temperature' parameter that decays over the time limit. In each SLSQP run, allow the solver to occasionally accept a state with a lower sum of radii with probability e^(\Delta / T). This is intended to help the solver escape local optima where circles are 'jammed' in a non-optimal configuration.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to be $\sum w_i r_i$ where $w_i$ is inversely proportional to the radius $r_i$. This encourages the solver to find a balanced distribution of large and small circles, preventing the solver from over-focusing on one large circle at the expense of many smaller circles that could fill the remaining gaps more efficiently.
backlog.title: Variable Radius Weights for Stability

backlog.spec: Implement a two-phase approach: Phase 1 uses SLSQP to optimize both centers and radii. Phase 2 takes the best configuration from Phase 1, fixes the centers $c_i$, and runs a second SLSQP pass (or a simpler iterative solver) only on the radii $r_i$. This separates the geometric arrangement from the sizing, potentially finding a more optimal size distribution for a given layout.
backlog.title: Two-Phase Radius Optimization (Fixed Centers)

backlog.spec: While keeping the hard constraints for the final check, add a soft penalty term to the objective: $-\sum r_i - \lambda \sum \text{overlap}(i, j)^2$. This 'pushes' the solver away from the boundaries of the feasible region during the search, making it more likely to find 'roomy' configurations that are easier to refine in the repair step.
backlog.title: Weighted Overlap Penalty during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Modify the restart logic. If a solve fails to improve the sum of radii significantly, take the best centers found so far, shrink all radii by a factor of 0.9, and run a new SLSQP pass. This allows the solver to 'relax' the packing and then try to grow the radii again in a new local basin.
backlog.title: Shrink-and-Grow Restart

backlog.spec: Instead of random centers, initialize centers by placing $n$ points and using a simple force-directed layout (or a few iterations of a gradient descent) to maximize the minimum distance between any two points. This creates a 'spread out' initial configuration which is often a better starting point for packing problems than uniform random distribution.
backlog.title: Max-Min Distance Initialization

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, instead of a constant shrink factor, calculate the shrink factor $s$ as a function of the overlap magnitude. For small overlaps, use a larger $s$ (closer to 1.0), and for large overlaps, use a smaller $s$. This prevents the repair step from over-shrinking radii when they only slightly violate the constraint.
backlog.title: Adaptive Shrink Factor

backlog.spec: Instead of one long SLSQP run, break the time into 5 segments. In each segment, solve for the radii $r_i$ while keeping centers $c_i$ fixed, then solve for centers $c_i$ while keeping radii $r_i$ fixed (but scaled up slightly). This alternating approach can explore the state space more thoroughly than joint optimization.
backlog.title: Iterative Radius Expansion (GRE)

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, instead of always picking the first (or maximum) overlap, randomly pick one of the top 3 largest overlaps to shrink. Run this for a fixed number of iterations. This introduces stochasticity into the repair process, which can help find different valid configurations from the same near-valid packing.
backlog.title: Multi-Seed Repair

backlog.spec: After a successful SLSQP solve that satisfies all constraints, attempt to 'inflate' the radii. Specifically, add a small epsilon (e.g., 1e-5) to all radii, then run a brief SLSQP pass (e.g., 50 iterations) with the same centers but the new larger radii as the starting point. If the solver fails to find a valid packing, discard the inflation and keep the previous valid state.
backlog.title: Stochastic Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed Gaussian noise (0.02) when reusing the best centers, scale the noise standard deviation based on the current 'best' sum of radii. As the sum of radii increases (approaching the target), reduce the noise standard deviation to perform more localized refinement in the high-quality regions of the configuration space.
backlog.title: Adaptive Perturbation Size

backlog.spec: Before starting the SLSQP, sort the initial radii in descending order. This forces the optimizer to prioritize the placement and size of larger circles first, which is a known heuristic for dense circle packing. The solver should then proceed to optimize the positions and radii of the smaller circles.
backlog.title: Greedy Radius Re-ordering

backlog.spec: Implement a time-aware iteration cap. Divide the 30s budget into phases. In the first 70% of the time, use a high MAX_ITER (e.g., 300) to explore. In the remaining 30% of the time, if the solver is still running, decrease the MAX_ITER dynamically or switch to a faster, less precise solver to ensure a valid packing is returned before the limit.
backlog.title: Dynamic Iteration Budgeting

backlog.spec: Modify the SLSQP objective to maximize $\sum r_i$ while adding a small penalty term for the variance of the radii (e.g., $- \lambda \	ext{Var}(r)$). This encourages the solver to find a diverse set of circle sizes, which often fills gaps more efficiently than circles of nearly identical sizes.
backlog.title: Radius-First Soft Constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the current _repair function. Instead of just shrinking the most overlapping pair, identify all pairs $(i, j)$ where $r_i + r_j > d_{ij}$ and shrink both $r_i$ and $r_j$ proportionally to the overlap amount. Repeat this until all overlaps are below a very small tolerance (e.g., 1e-11).
backlog.title: Iterative Local Repair

backlog.spec: Maintain the best 'valid' packing found so far. Every 5 restarts, instead of just perturbing the best centers, perform a 'greedy growth' step: keep the centers of the best packing fixed, and run an SLSQP solve that only optimizes the radii $r_i$ to be as large as possible until they hit the boundaries or each other.
backlog.title: Best-State Re-injection

backlog.spec: Instead of applying Gaussian noise to the best centers, apply a small displacement to each center $c_i$ in the direction of the nearest neighbor $c_j$, but in the opposite direction. This 'pushes' circles away from each other slightly, potentially creating room for radii expansion in subsequent SLSQP steps.
backlog.title: Voronoi-Inspired Jitter

backlog.spec: Implement a cooling schedule for the restarts. Start with a high exploration rate (large noise on centers). As the time limit approaches, linearly decrease the noise standard deviation and increase the probability of reusing the 'best' configuration, focusing the final seconds on local refinement.
backlog.title: Temperature-Scaled restarts

backlog.spec: Initialize the radii such that $\sum \pi r_i^2$ is slightly less than the area of the unit square (e.g., 0.9 * 1.0). Use a distribution that favors larger circles (e.g., power law) and then let SLSQP optimize the final positions and radii. This provides a much denser starting point than uniform random radii.
backlog.title: Area-Proportional Initialization

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP solve, add a small random component to the radii values in the objective function (e.g., $\sum (r_i + \epsilon_i)$) or slightly perturb the radii before each SLSQP call while keeping centers fixed, to explore the local surface of the radius sum more broadly.
backlog.title: Stochastic Radius Growth

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP solve, fix the centers $c$ and solve a linear program (or a simple iterative greedy step) to maximize $\sum r_i$ subject to $r_i + r_j \le \text{dist}(c_i, c_j)$ and $r_i \le \min(c_{i,x}, 1-c_{i,x}, c_{i,y}, 1-c_{i,y})$. This can be done iteratively since the constraints are linear in $r$.
backlog.title: Radius-only LP Refinement

backlog.spec: Before starting the SLSQP, sort the initial radii such that the largest radii are assigned to the 'best' (most open) parts of the square. Specifically, try a few different permutations of radii (e.g., largest to smallest, random, and largest-to-smallest-center-distance) and pick the best.
backlog.title: Greedy Radius Re-ordering

backlog.spec: When restarting from the best center configuration, instead of a uniform Gaussian jitter, move each center $c_i$ slightly in a direction that moves it away from its nearest neighbors (the Voronoi cell boundary direction) to escape local minima.
backlog.title: Voronoi-inspired Jitter

backlog.spec: Adjust the standard deviation of the jitter applied to reused centers based on how much the sum of radii improved in the last step. If the improvement was small, increase the jitter; if large, decrease it to perform a local fine-grained search.
backlog.title: Adaptive Perturbation Size

backlog.spec: Initialize the radii $r_i$ such that the total area $\sum \pi r_i^2$ is close to the maximum possible packing density (e.g., 0.85). Use a distribution that favors larger circles but ensures they aren't so large that they are impossible to pack.
backlog.title: Area-Proportional Initialization

backlog.spec: Replace the current `_repair` with a local search: in each iteration, pick the pair with the maximum overlap and move the center of the smaller circle slightly away from the larger circle while simultaneously shrinking its radius just enough to resolve the overlap.
backlog.title: Iterative Local Repair

backlog.spec: Dynamically adjust `MAX_ITER`. During the first 70% of the time budget, use a lower `MAX_ITER` to explore many configurations. In the final 30% of the time, use a very high `MAX_ITER` on the best found configuration to polish the result.
backlog.title: Time-proportional Iterations

backlog.spec: Change the objective function to maximize $\sum w_i r_i$ where $w_i$ is a weight. Start with $w_i=1$ for all $i$, and slowly increase weights for smaller circles over the course of the SLSQP iterations to see if a more balanced distribution of radii yields a better sum.
backlog.title: Variable Radius Weights

incumbent.description: Keep the best centre configuration found so far and, on each restart with probability 1/2, start SLSQP from that configuration plus small Gaussian noise instead of uniform random centres.

memo: Helped: only slot 2 (keep the best centre configuration and restart or perturb from it with some probability): -2.9327, delta -0.0074. It is the sole accepted change and the incumbent. Did not help: initialisation changes (log-normal radii -2.9284/-2.9244; Poisson disc -2.9325; radii at TARGET_SUM/n -2.9337), multi-pass SLSQP (-2.9313, -2.9332), jitter and re-solve (-2.9312), randomised repair (-2.9319), iteration-cap schedules (+0.0000), soft penalties (-2.9310, -2.9331). The pure penalty objective failed badly (-2.1510). Near noise (sd about 0.0034) but best-looking: Metropolis temperature (-2.9352), basin-hop (-2.9349), and TARGET_SUM/n init (-2.9337). Replicate these on top of slot 2 before judging them. Lesson: SLSQP hard constraints work, and init, schedule and repair tweaks sit near noise. Many ideas were aborted as duplicates, which wasted slots. Next: tune the perturbation size and restart probability of the slot 2 scheme, and try removing the smallest circle and reinserting it in the largest hole, or swapping two circles. Keep the code simple.
